page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor. The configuration provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores at a 2.5 GHz clock speed, operating on the x86_64 architecture with multithreading enabled. The system includes 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware-level instruction support includes AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 extensions are absent.

A key differentiator for the m5ad variant is the inclusion of 2400 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, multi-core computational throughput is stable, reflected by an average multi-core PassMark CPU score of 37,068.04 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,518.0. Cryptographic throughput demonstrates higher relative strength, with PassMark CPU encryption ranking in the top 25 percent at 51,288.39. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into the bottom 10 percent, shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 731.0 and a single-core stress-ng rating of 591.38.

The primary tradeoff of this instance rests on its core generation. While per-core single-threaded execution and larger-scale LLM inference speeds are constrained, the high density of 64 vCPUs, 256 GB of memory, and fast local NVMe storage deliver strong multi-threaded resource allocation without the added costs of separated network storage. This profile suits multi-threaded batch workloads, caching systems, distributed data processing, relational and NoSQL databases requiring scratch space, and containerized microservice architectures.
description: Amazon Web Services m5ad.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by a 2.5 GHz AMD EPYC 7571 processor on the Nitro hypervisor. The system delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs, 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, and 2400 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage, supplemented by a 12 Gbps baseline network capacity. Benchmark metrics show standard multi-core performance alongside strong cryptographic execution, achieving an encryption score in the top 25 percent. However, single-core processing metrics, such as a Geekbench score of 731.0, place it in the lower tiers for single-threaded throughput. The combination of dense multi-core processing, substantial memory, and integrated high-speed local storage makes the m5ad.16xlarge cost-efficient for parallel data processing, database servers with high temporary storage requirements, web serving clusters, and multi-tenant container fleets.
